_comment: GH#142: Hedault's enchanting. requires {item, gold} gates show-locked with the item/gold labels; effects = gold-fee + remove_item base + item variant (the shipped swap triple -- ZERO engine). Canon voice: exacting, formal, no haggling, hates being touched. Book-17 bar: no Vol 8+ content.

hub.speaker: Hedault
hub.text: State the item and keep your hands where I can see them. First I appraise. Then I correct, if correction is warranted, and I charge exactly what the work is worth.

options.text: The traveler's charm. Improve it. (20 gold)
The hunter's fang. Make it more than a trophy. (35 gold)
The wardstone bead. Set it true. (40 gold)
The guardian's fragment. I'm told you'd want to see it.
Just looking.

options._comment: Spec 4 (Task 6.2) INVRISIL CAPSTONE. Gated on the Invrisil chain's terminal (brothers_job_done) + spine_started, hidden once read. Revisit arm on the hub, not a chain tail, so a save that already closed the Brothers' job reaches it (spec 8). He knows CRAFT -- a fed draw versus a set one -- and refuses to speculate past his own trade, so the assembled picture is never spoken here.
options.text: You've stopped mid-appraisal. What are you looking at?

options._comment: v0.16 I1 (#306, ruling 1). Appended LAST and accomplishment-gated, so it is HIDDEN in hedault_fragment_start and spine_reach_start -- the 5-row options pin and spine_reach's blind `move down 5` both stay exact, zero re-pins.
options.text: A lady's heirloom. She was told you'd refuse it.

door_reading.speaker: Hedault
door_reading._comment: The 'catalogued exactly once before' callback is a TRADER's line: it names the fragment this player handed him, so it may only render if they did. Base is the same read without the claim.
door_reading.text: Hold still. There is a residue on your sleeve I do not see twice in a decade. Ruin warding. A set ward would have gone quiet years ago; this one is fed, and the draw is live. Looking costs nothing.

text_variants.text: Hold still. There is a residue on your sleeve I have catalogued exactly once before — in this shop, on the fragment you handed me. Ruin warding. A set ward would have gone quiet years ago; this one is fed, and the draw is live. Looking costs nothing.

options.text: Go on, then.
Another time. Keep the reading.

door_reading_verdict._comment: HIS OWN PIECE ONLY (spec 4): the set-versus-fed distinction is an enchanter's read, and he stops exactly where the fragment_study node stops. The source of the draw is named as unknown, never as a seal.
door_reading_verdict.speaker: Hedault
door_reading_verdict.text: A set ward holds a shape. A fed ward has to be sourced, continuously, from somewhere with capacity. Whoever hung that frame did not hang it alone, and I have measured what it pulls. Nothing in your pantry pulls that. I will not speculate further in a shop. Bring me the setting when you know, and I will price the work correctly.

options.text: Understood.

work_done.speaker: Hedault
work_done.text: Done. The work is correct; it is on the cloth and the fee is as quoted. Do not thank me or shake my hand. And keep it away from street enchanters afterward.

options.text: Understood.

fragment_study.speaker: Hedault
fragment_study._comment: b6 #221 the trade-by-CHOICE close + the door-chain lore line. SPOILER BAR: oblique — one school of warding, no names, no volumes. The player gives up guarding_ward (the fragment's combat skill) for the wardstone + the read; keeping the fragment is the equally valid choice.
fragment_study.text: Hold. Turn it — there. Ruin warding, and well past apprentice work. The same discipline set the frame you woke on your pantry door; one school, long dissolved, and I will not guess at names in a shop. The setting is yours. The fragment stays with someone who can read it properly.

options.text: Fair trade.

heirloom_bench.speaker: Hedault
heirloom_bench._comment: He will not work until the lie is named. The two SKILL arms are SEPARATE single-key options (test_content rejects {skill, item} -- pisces_seal.json:112).
heirloom_bench.text: Set it on the cloth. Do not hand it to me. I have looked at it twice already and I will not cut a mount until somebody in this transaction says the true thing out loud: that stone is glass, cut well, sold badly, and about forty years old. I will not cut a mount over a lie. It is half-drawn on the bench behind me, and it stays half-drawn until I hear it.

options.text: "She knows. She's known since she was nineteen. She wants the setting held properly, and the stone left as it is."
[Appraise Goods] Read it out with him, weight by weight.
[Detect Magic] Follow the ward-line to where it wants to sit.
"Somebody swapped it. Who buys a stone like that?"
"I'll come back with an answer."

heirloom_truth.speaker: Hedault
heirloom_truth.text: Good. Then it goes on the order in those words and the price changes, downward, because glass takes less holding than a stone does. A mount for glass is not a lesser commission. It is a different one, and I would rather be told than discover it at the bench.

options.text: "She'll be glad of the price."

bench_assist.speaker: Hedault
bench_assist.text: Stand where I put you and keep your hands flat on the cloth. Now read it back to me. If you are wrong, I will stop you. There. The ward wants to sit under the setting. It has ignored the stone from the first weighing. Keep your hands flat while I mark the line.

options.text: "Understood."

fence_pointer.speaker: Hedault
fence_pointer._comment: Pointer only -- banks nothing; the FIGHT counter comes off the alley encounter's on_victory.
fence_pointer.text: Forty years ago somebody took the stone and left the glass, and did it well enough that the family never thought to ask. Do not expect the thief to still hold it. Stones of that quality get sold on. There is a man with a back door off the alleys and a ledger he would not show the Watch. I do not go there. You have the address. I have a mount to cut.

options.text: "That's enough."
